Menu path: Home -> Sales History -> select the original sale -> Return

A Posnic return starts from the original sale, preserves its commercial evidence, puts tracked quantities back into stock and records either a partial or full return; adding a replacement item turns the same workspace into an exchange.

## Before Accepting a Return

Check | Why it matters | Operator action

Original bill | The return must be tied to the sale that set price, tax, discount, customer and payment evidence. | Search Sales History by the bill details; do not create a negative new sale.

Remaining quantity | Posnic rejects zero, negative or already-returned quantities and prevents returning more than remains on the bill. | Check earlier returns and count the quantity physically received.

Item condition | Tracked stock is added back automatically even when an item is damaged or unsellable. | Follow shop policy for quarantine or a later stock adjustment and write a reason.

"title": "Install Posnic POS and Complete First Launch",

"content": "Install Posnic POS and Complete First Launch

Menu path: Download package -> first launch wizard -> Dashboard

Use this before training cashiers: install the app, understand demo versus local data, finish shop setup, and confirm the dashboard is ready.

## Choose Demo or Local Install

Start with the browser demo when you only need to learn screen names and the shape of the workflow. Treat all demo data as disposable.

Use a local installer when you need to test the exact computer, printer, scanner, cashier routine, tax setup, backup path and day close that the shop will actually use.

Do not enter real customer, payment, tax or supplier data in the public demo.

Repeat every accepted demo step in a local install before production.

Keep the package name, version and operating system in the shop setup record.

## Install and Start

The packaged Posnic app brings its own local runtime and database path. A cashier should not need to install a separate database or web server for normal local use.

Download Posnic from the official download page for the computer operating system.

Run the installer or portable package using the shop owner account policy.

Allow first launch to finish creating local app data and database files.

If the operating system asks for confirmation, verify the package source before allowing it.

When the login or first-run wizard appears, stop and enter approved shop details instead of temporary live values.

## Complete First-Run Setup

First-run setup is not just a technical step. It creates names, defaults and controls that later appear on receipts, reports and staff screens.

Use the exact shop name and receipt address approved by the business owner.

The signed claims now additionally require a bounded canonical token shape, scalar hexadecimal nonce, supported action type and integer expiry. MongoDB uses explicit equality for nonce/type and checks the saved draft expiry. Execution uses the claimed database row's type and payload. Invalid claims, even signed ones, cannot reach the database. |

| [1039: file race](https://github.com/Posnic/POS/security/code-scanning/1039) | Recovery evidence is opened once, inspected with `fstat` and read from the same descriptor.
